title: Environment arrangement cannot hide an installed object's built-in tabs (attachments, approvals, activity stream)
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY

Filed as a `finding` by seat `repo:objectstack#2` from l2-review#4 record 7084262686 on PR #36517 (card #36498, fork 3). Not triaged; not claimed.

## What

PR #36517 lets the base's paired `.custom` package write `relatedLists` for an installed object, and `{ list, hidden: true }` hides a relationship tab. The three built-in tabs (`sys_attachment`, `sys_approval_request`, `sys_activity`) cannot be hidden this way:

- an unlisted built-in tab still shows;
- `hidden` is refused on a built-in entry;
- the environment cannot patch the object's own `enable` keys.

So an environment administrator has no way to hide the attachments tab or the activity stream of an installed object.

Card #36498 item 1 lets the list name the built-in tabs, and item 4 says hiding is written. L2 judged this a maintainer question: additive, and not blocking #36517.

## Likely shape

Accept `{ list: 'sys_attachment' | 'sys_approval_request' | 'sys_activity', hidden: true }` in the `.custom` arrangement only, read by `deriveRelatedLists` and the default page synthesis. The open question is whether that is a second switch beside the object's own `enable` keys. It is a product decision.

Re-check: `ObjectExtensionRelatedListEntrySchema` refuses `hidden` on a built-in name.
